In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the visual process.
a cyclic GMP-dependent, light-suppressible conductance in the rod outer segment membrane.
the mechanism of visual transduction in the rod outer segment of the vertebrate retina, a process that is thought to be triggered by a light flash and to be mediated by the cyclic nucleotide cGMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that a cGMP-dependent light-sensitive conductance can be recorded from the plasma membrane of rod outer segments and that this conductance can be suppressed by light.
the cGOMP-sensitive conductance is the light-sensitive conduct- ance.
the patch experiments have shown that cGMP modulates the light-sensitive conductances by directly opening and closing ion channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the patch experiments were indeed measuring a cGMP-sensitive, light-suppressible conductance in the outer segment plasma membrane; that this conductance was a significant fraction of the total light-sensitive conductance; and that cGMP was probably the physiological mediator of phototransduction.

the cG MP-sensitive conductance in excised patches of outer segment plasma membrane is identical in electrical properties to the light-sensitive conduct-gance and can be suppressed by a flash of light in the presence of both ATP and GTP.
the cGMO-sensitive conductance in excised patches from rod outer segments is the same as the light-sensitive conductances in the intact rod outer segment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light-sensitive conductances are present in the outer segment plasma membrane and can be suppressed by a flash of light.
the patch conductance is light-suppressible and therefore is likely to be the same as the light-sensitive conductances in the intact outer segments.
cGMP is the direct mediator of the light-sensitive current in retinal rods.
